analysis: The change to scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py is test-only and has two parts. First, a comment at line 132 now cites watchdog commit d6d257c2 instead of 31236c54. Second, test_watchdog_rescues_only_this_repositorys_routed_runs (lines 949-953) gains a regression assertion. It checks that the copied watchdog workflow body never passes a run/job listing to jq as a command-line argument (`--arg`/`--argjson ... "$all"`, `"$more"`, `"$runs"`, `"$jobs"` or `"$cancelled"`). The stated reason is E2BIG ("Argument list too long") on large listings. This is an availability hardening check for the CI watchdog, which sits outside the provider threat model's asset and trust-boundary scope (TB-002 to TB-014). It does not touch provider code, attestation, encryption, the prefix cache (T-041) or any runtime control. The new check only adds a test constraint on the workflow text and weakens nothing. The existing tests keep their guards: routed lanes use read-only permissions, forks never contact the plane, the unrouted release and credentialed workflows keep literal blacksmith runners and no darkbloom labels, and the router is isolated with `permissions: {}`. The test's regex is a heuristic: it matches only the exact quoted-variable pattern, so it would not catch every way of passing a listing as an argument. That is a coverage limit of the test, not a security regression. I could not see the watchdog workflow file itself, since it is in another unit or batch; whether its actual content matches the new assertion is unverified and is a CI-correctness question rather than a security one. No findings.
